words.defJa: うそや計略で人をだます

cards.ja: 歴史の試験では、「トロイの木馬」が敵をあざむく策の例としてよく引かれます。ただし、これは史実として確認された出来事ではなく、古代の叙事詩に語られる伝説です。出題文に「伝説」と「史実」の区別があるかどうかを、まず確かめましょう。そうすれば、選択肢の言い回しに惑わされることも減ります。歴史の問題は、史実と伝承の線引きを問う設問が意外に多く、それを知らないと引っかかりやすいのです。
cards.en: In history exams, the “Trojan horse” is often cited as an example of a ruse to deceive the enemy. However, this is not an event confirmed as historical fact but a legend told in an ancient epic. First check whether the question text distinguishes between “legend” and “historical fact.” Then you will be less misled by the phrasing of the answer choices. Surprisingly many history questions ask where to draw the line between fact and tradition, and you are easily tripped up if you do not know this.

words.defJa: 匙。薬を量る小さな道具

cards.ja: 医療の現場では、回復は難しいと医師がさじを投げた患者が、のちに歩けるようになった例が報告されることがある。この表現は、医者が薬を量る匙を投げ出して治療を断念したことに由来するとされる。奇跡は当てにできないものの、重い負傷のあとでも、本人の意欲が回復の足取りを左右するという指摘は多い。それでも、希望を語る言葉は、医療者の側にも求められている。回復の道のりに、確かな正解はない。
cards.en: In medicine, there are sometimes reports of patients whom doctors had given up on as unlikely to recover later becoming able to walk. This expression is said to derive from a doctor throwing down the spoon used to measure medicine and abandoning treatment. Though miracles cannot be counted on, many point out that even after a serious injury the patient's will affects the pace of recovery. Even so, words that speak of hope are also demanded of medical staff. There is no sure right answer on the road to recovery.

words.defJa: あやまりの気持ちを伝えること

cards.ja: 謝罪の表現は、場面に応じて使い分けます。「すみません」は軽く、「申し訳ありません」は丁寧で、メールで「おわび申し上げます」と書けば、きちんと謝る気持ちが伝わります。ただし、大げさに謝りすぎると、かえって誠意を疑われかねません。短く、具体的に、何について謝るのかを示すのがコツです。謝るときは、理由と今後の対応を一言添えるだけで、同じ言葉でも受け取られ方がまるで変わってきます。
cards.en: Expressions of apology are used differently depending on the situation. “Sumimasen” is light, “moushiwake arimasen” is polite, and writing “owabi moushiagemasu” in an email conveys a proper feeling of apology. However, apologizing too extravagantly may, on the contrary, lead people to doubt your sincerity. The knack is to be brief and specific about what you are apologizing for. When apologizing, merely adding a word about the reason and what you will do next changes how the same words are received.

cards.enTarget: “Sumimasen” is light, “moushiwake arimasen” is polite, and writing “owabi moushiagemasu” in an email conveys a proper feeling of apology.

words.defJa: 限度いっぱいまで満ちること

cards.ja: 一日に受け取る通知の数が増え続け、現代人の注意力はすでに飽和状態にあると指摘する研究者は少なくない。画面を見ていないときですら、人は次の通知を待ってしまうという。この状態が続くと、深く考える時間は失われ、脳への負担も増す一方である。通知を切ることは、小さいながらも有効な対策だ。情報を足すよりも、入り口を減らして頭に静かな余白を取り戻すことが、いま本当に求められているのかもしれない。
cards.en: Not a few researchers point out that modern people's attention is already saturated as the number of notifications received each day keeps growing. Even when not looking at the screen, people reportedly end up waiting for the next one. If this continues, time for deep thinking is lost, and the strain on the brain only increases. Turning off notifications is a small but effective countermeasure. What is truly needed now may be not adding information but reducing entry points and recovering a quiet margin in the head.

words.defJa: 自分をすぐれていると思い込む

cards.ja: インドの古い教えには、自分の力に酔ってうぬぼれる者への戒めが繰り返し出てきます。たとえば『バガヴァッド・ギーター』は、行為の結果に執着するなと説きます。成功は自分だけの手柄ではなく、無数の条件が重なった結果にすぎません。そう気づいた人は、結果に一喜一憂せず、目の前の務めを貫けるのです。謙虚さとは、自分を小さく見ることではなく、自分を支える条件の多さを正しく見ることなのです。
cards.en: Ancient Indian teachings repeatedly warn against those who get drunk on their own power and become conceited. The Bhagavad Gita, for example, teaches not to cling to the results of action. Success is not solely your own credit; it is merely the outcome of countless conditions coinciding. A person who realizes this can stay the course of the duty before them without swinging between joy and sorrow over results. Humility is not seeing yourself as small but seeing correctly how many conditions support you.

cards.enTarget: Ancient Indian teachings repeatedly warn against those who get drunk on their own power and become conceited.

words.defJa: 作りがしっかりして壊れにくいこと

cards.ja: 半導体の世界では、車に載せるチップに求められるのは、速さよりもまず頑丈なつくりです。炎天下の車内は想像以上に高温になり、家電向けの部品なら数日で壊れかねません。だから自動車メーカーは、十年以上使える寿命と高い信頼性を要求します。派手な性能競争の陰で、地味な丈夫さが産業を支えているのです。性能の数字ばかりが注目されがちですが、止まらずに動き続ける性質こそ、社会を支える技術の条件なのです。
cards.en: In the semiconductor world, what is demanded of chips that go into cars is, first of all, a sturdy build rather than speed. A car interior under a blazing sun gets hotter than you would imagine, and parts designed for home appliances might break within days. That is why automakers demand a lifespan of over ten years and high reliability. Behind the flashy performance race, plain toughness is what supports the industry. Attention tends to go to performance figures, but the quality of running without stopping is the very condition of technology that supports society.

cards.tipJa: 「頑丈な体」「頑丈な作り」。壊れにくさ。人にも物にも使う。
cards.enTarget: In the semiconductor world, what is demanded of chips that go into cars is, first of all, a sturdy build rather than speed.

words.defJa: 物でいっぱいになり、ほかのことに使えなくなる

cards.ja: 日本語には『手がふさがっている』という表現がある。両手に荷物を抱えて文字どおり動かせない場合はもちろん、仕事に追われて頼みごとを受けられない場合にも使われる。後者は前者からの類推でできた比喩であり、文脈によって意味が分かれる。学習者にとっては、同じ形が二つの状況にまたがる点が、理解を難しくする一因となっている。辞書を引いても、こうした慣用的な広がりまでは載っていないことが多い。
cards.en: Japanese has the expression 'te ga fusagatte iru,' literally 'my hands are occupied'. It is used not only when you are carrying luggage in both arms and literally cannot move, but also when you are swamped with work and cannot take on a request. The latter is a metaphor formed by analogy with the former, and the meaning splits depending on context. For learners, the fact that one form spans two situations is one reason it is hard to grasp. Even if you look it up in a dictionary, such idiomatic extensions are often not listed.

words.defJa: 力が加わると、すぐ壊れたり崩れたりしやすい

cards.ja: 最先端のAIでも、実はもろい一面があります。たとえば、パンダの画像に人間には見えないほどの細かなノイズを加えるだけで、モデルがテナガザルだと自信たっぷりに答えてしまう例が研究で示されています。これが『敵対的サンプル』と呼ばれる現象です。性能が高いからといって、安全だとは限らないのです。だからこそ、実際に使う前に、わざと意地悪な入力を何度も与えて試す検査が欠かせないのです。
cards.en: Even cutting-edge AI turns out to have a fragile side. For example, research has shown that merely adding noise too fine for humans to see to an image of a panda can make a model answer with confidence that it is a gibbon. This phenomenon is called an 'adversarial sample'. High performance does not necessarily mean it is safe. That is why, before real use, tests that deliberately feed it nasty inputs again and again are indispensable.

words.defJa: 急に。また、すぐには（打ち消しと共に）

cards.ja: 『にわか雨』が突然降る雨を指すように、この語は本来、物事が急に起きるさまを表していました。それが『にわかに信じがたい話』という形になると、『すぐには』という別の意味が顔を出します。後ろに打ち消しの言葉が続くと、急にではなく容易にという読みになるのです。新聞の見出しから日常会話に至るまで、この用法は広く見られます。同じ語でも、肯定か否定かで意味が食い違う点には注意が要ります。
cards.en: Just as 'niwaka ame' refers to rain that falls suddenly, this word originally described things happening all at once. Yet in the form 'niwaka ni shinjigatai hanashi,' another meaning, 'not readily,' shows its face. When a negation follows, it reads as 'easily' rather than 'suddenly'. This usage is common everywhere, from newspaper headlines to everyday conversation. Take care that the meaning diverges depending on whether the sentence is affirmative or negative.

words.defJa: 水などを寄せつけず、はね返す

cards.ja: 古代ギリシアの陶工は、壺の表面に黒い粘土の液で絵を描き、焼いて黒く光る像を浮かび上がらせた。仕上がった陶器の肌は、水をはじくほどなめらかだった。その光沢は、実用品にすぎない壺を、神話の場面を語る画布へと変えたのである。日用の器といえども、手のかけ方ひとつで、時代を超えて人の目をひきつけることができる。それは、粘土という素朴な素材が二千年以上前に到達した、ひとつの完成形でもあった。
cards.en: Ancient Greek potters painted pictures on the surface of vessels with a liquid of black clay, then fired them so that shining black figures stood out. The finished ceramic skin was so smooth that it repelled water. That luster turned a vase, a mere utensil, into a canvas telling scenes from myth. Even an everyday vessel can, depending on the care lavished on it, hold people's eyes across the ages. It was also a form of perfection that the humble material of clay had reached more than two thousand years ago.

words.defJa: 墨やインクが紙に広がって、輪郭がぼやける

cards.ja: 万年筆で書いた文字が、湿った紙の上ではにじむことがある。不思議なことに、手書きの文章はそのにじみまでが、書き手の気持ちを伝える言葉の一部になる。画面上の文字は、どれほど整っていても、そうした余白や揺らぎを持たない。ゆえに、私たちは便利さと引き換えに、読みとれたはずの感情の一断面を失っているのではないだろうか。だからこそ、あえて手書きで手紙を書く人が今も絶えないのだろう。
cards.en: Characters written with a fountain pen may blur on damp paper. Strangely, in handwriting even that blur becomes part of the language that conveys the writer's feelings. Characters on a screen, however neat, have no such margin or wavering. Hence we may be losing, in exchange for convenience, one cross-section of emotion that we could once have read. That is perhaps why people who deliberately write letters by hand have still not died out.

words.defJa: 物事の全体のうち、一部分を切り取って見た姿

cards.ja: AIの精度が95パーセントって聞くと、すごいなって思うじゃないですか。でも、それってテストに使った問題という、全体のほんの一断面を切り取った数字にすぎないんです。実際の現場では、サンプルの偏りも、質問のされ方も、使う人の慣れ具合や期待も、まるで違うことがよくあります。だから、数字を見たら、『これは何を切り取ったものなのか』って、一回立ち止まるのがおすすめですよ。
cards.en: When you hear that an AI's accuracy is 95 percent, you think, wow, don't you? But that is only a number cutting out one cross-section of the whole, namely the questions used in the test. In the real world, the bias of the samples, the way questions get asked and how practiced the users are are often completely different. So when you see a number, I recommend stopping once to think, 'what exactly was this cut from?'

words.defJa: 結んだものが、ひとりでにゆるんで解ける

cards.ja: 形が類似した『ひもをほどく』と『ひもがほどける』は、同じ結果を、人の意志の有無で言い分けています。前者は誰かが解く他動詞、後者は自然にゆるんでしまう自動詞です。日本語は、起きたことを自分の責任から切り離して語りたいとき、この自動詞を好む傾向があると日本語学ではよく言われます。『割ってしまった』にしろ『割れてしまった』にしろ事実は同じですが、後者のほうがずっと角が立ちません。
cards.en: 'Himo o hodoku' and 'himo ga hodokeru,' which are similar in form, express the same result while distinguishing the presence or absence of human intention. The former is a transitive verb meaning someone unties it, the latter an intransitive verb meaning it loosens on its own. Japanese is often said in Japanese linguistics to tend to favor this intransitive when it wants to describe what happened apart from one's own responsibility. Whether you say 'I broke it' or 'it broke,' the fact is the same, but the latter does not ruffle feathers.

words.defJa: 経験で蓄えた、物事をうまく行うための技術や秘訣

cards.ja: 機械翻訳の精度が急速に上がるなか、翻訳の現場では、人間が蓄えてきたノウハウをどう残すかが課題になっている。専門用語の訳し分けや読者に合わせた文体の調整は、辞書に載らない経験の積み重ねだからだ。翻訳会社の中には、機械の訳文を人が直した修正例を整理し、社内で共有する取り組みを始めたところもある。とはいえ、原文の意図と食い違う訳をいかに見抜くかは、依然として人の目に頼らざるを得ない。
cards.en: As the accuracy of machine translation rises rapidly, how to preserve the know-how that humans have accumulated has become a challenge in translation workplaces. Distinguishing technical terms and adjusting style to the reader are accumulations of experience that appear in no dictionary. Some translation companies have begun organizing examples where people corrected machine output and sharing them internally. Even so, spotting translations that diverge from the original's intent still has to rely on human eyes.

words.defJa: 苦労や工夫をして、どうにか目的を果たすさま

cards.ja: 締め切りの前日になっても、課題に手をつけられない学生は少なくない。心理学では、先延ばしは意志の弱さというより、不快な感情への対処の失敗だと説明されている。徹夜でなんとか提出にこぎつけた経験が、かえって悪い習慣を強めると指摘する研究者もいる。順序を決めて最初の五分だけ始めるという対策は、シンプルながら有効だとされる。完璧な状態を待たず、まず雑な下書きを一行書いてみるのも有効である。
cards.en: Not a few students still cannot touch their assignment even the day before the deadline. In psychology, procrastination is explained less as weakness of will than as a failure to cope with unpleasant feelings. Some researchers point out that the experience of somehow managing to hand something in after an all-nighter actually reinforces the bad habit. Deciding an order and starting with just the first five minutes is said to be simple yet effective. Writing one rough line of a draft without waiting for perfect conditions is also effective.

cards.enTarget: Some researchers point out that the experience of somehow managing to hand something in after an all-nighter actually reinforces the bad habit.

words.defJa: 心配が消えて、安心して気持ちが軽くなる

cards.ja: ガンジス河のほとりで朝の祈りを眺めていたら、不思議とほっとしたんですよ。人でごった返して、牛もいて、鐘の音はうるさいくらいなのに、騒がしいどころか静けさすら感じたんです。たぶん、誰も私のことなんか気にしていない、という感覚が心地よかったんでしょうね。旅の間ずっと張りつめていた気持ちが、魂ごと洗われてゆるんだ気がしました。あの朝の感覚は、旅から戻った今でも、ときどきふっとよみがえってきます。
cards.en: Watching the morning prayers by the Ganges, I felt strangely relieved. It was crowded with people, there were cows, and the bells were loud, yet far from noisy, I even sensed a stillness. Probably it felt good to have the feeling that nobody cared about me. The tension I'd kept up throughout the trip seemed to ease, as if my very soul had been washed. Even now, back from the trip, that morning feeling sometimes comes back to me all of a sudden.

cards.enTarget: Watching the morning prayers by the Ganges, I felt strangely relieved.

words.defJa: 相手の要求や条件を、そのまま受け入れる

cards.ja: AI企業と各国政府の交渉では、政府の関与を認めて規制をどこまでのむかが最大の争点になっています。たとえば、学習データの出所を開示せよという要求を、企業が全面的に受け入れた例はまだ少ないのが実情です。開示すれば競合に手の内を明かすことになりかねないからです。とはいえ、信頼を得られなければ市場そのものが先細りになる恐れがあります。どこまで譲るかの線引きは、法務の問題ではなく、事業の将来像を決める経営判断でもあります。
cards.en: In negotiations between AI companies and governments, the biggest point of contention is how far to accept government involvement and swallow regulation. For example, there are still few cases in which a company has fully accepted a demand to disclose where its training data comes from. That is because disclosure could end up revealing its hand to competitors. Even so, without earning trust, the market itself risks shrinking. Where to draw the line on concessions is not merely a legal matter but a management decision that shapes the company's future.

words.defJa: 一部ではなく、全部そっくりそのままであるさま

cards.ja: 画像生成AIの学習には、公開データセットから選ばれた数十億枚の画像が使われたと報じられている。作品がまるまる学習に使われたとして、美術家らが開発企業を提訴する例が相次いだ。収集と学習が著作権法上の適法な利用に当たるかをめぐり、各国で議論が続いている。生成物が元の作品に類似している場合の扱いについても、判断は割れている。技術の進歩に法の整備が追いついていないことが、争いを長引かせている。
cards.en: It has been reported that billions of images selected from public datasets were used to train image-generating AI. A string of cases followed in which artists sued the developers, arguing that their works were used in training in their entirety. Debate continues in various countries over whether collection and training count as lawful use under copyright law. Judgments are also divided on how to treat outputs that resemble the original works. The fact that legal frameworks have not caught up with technological progress is prolonging the dispute.

words.defJa: 邪魔なものを残らず取り除くこと

cards.ja: 話し方の指導でよく言われるのが、口ぐせの一掃です。『えーと』『なんか』『やっぱり』といった言葉は、本人が気づかなくても、聞き手の耳に何度も引っかかり、話の説得力を損なわずにはおきません。まず録音して数え、次に一語ずつ減らしていく順序で進めると、数週間で話の印象がすっきり変わります。完全にゼロにする必要はなく、人前で話す大事な場面で、ほとんど出なくなれば十分です。
cards.en: What is often said in speech coaching is the sweeping away of verbal tics. Words like 'eeto,' 'nanka' and 'yappari,' even if the speaker doesn't notice, snag the listener's ear again and again and cannot fail to undermine the persuasiveness of the talk. Proceeding in the order of first recording and counting, then cutting back one word at a time, changes the impression of your speech within a few weeks. You need not bring it to zero; it is enough if the tics almost never appear at important moments in front of people.

words.defJa: 必要なものが十分に備わっておらず、欠けていること

cards.ja: AIが誤った判断を下すと、私たちはつい、モデルの性能不足を疑う。だが実際には、原因が学習データの不備にあることが少なくない。たとえば、特定の地域や年齢層に限定された記録で学んだ医療AIは、欠けた集団の患者に対して、精度が著しく下がる。これは技術の限界というより、データを集めた人間の設計の問題である。データの質を見直さないまま、モデルだけを改良しても、問題は繰り返される。
cards.en: When AI makes an incorrect judgment, we tend to doubt the model's insufficient performance. In fact, though, it is not rare for the cause to lie in flaws of the training data. For example, a medical AI trained on records limited to particular regions or age groups sees its accuracy drop markedly for patients of the groups left out. This is less a limit of technology than a problem in the design by the humans who collected the data. If the quality of the data is not reviewed, improving only the model will lead to the problem recurring.

words.defJa: 物事の成り行きや、そのときの状況

cards.ja: 予想外の事態に直面したとき、人は普段の癖が一気にむき出しになります。慌てて頑固に同じやり方を繰り返す人もいれば、すぐに他人を非難して責任を逃れようとする人もいます。ところが、本当に危機に強い人は、まず状況を言葉にして、順序を決めることから始めます。感情に巻き込まれながらも、ひとつ離れて眺める視点を持てるかどうかが、分かれ目になるのです。危機の最中にこそ、人の本質は静かに現れるものです。
cards.en: When facing an unexpected situation, people's usual habits are laid bare all at once. Some flounder and stubbornly repeat the same method, while others immediately blame someone else to escape responsibility. People who are truly strong in a crisis, however, begin by putting the situation into words and deciding an order. Whether you can, while caught up in emotion, still keep a viewpoint that watches from a step apart is the dividing line. It is in the very midst of a crisis that a person's essence quietly shows itself.

words.defJa: 大きな声で、相手を激しく悪く言う

cards.ja: ネット上で見知らぬ相手をののしる投稿は、なぜこれほど後を絶たないのか。研究者の間では、顔が見えないことで自制が弱まる『脱抑制効果』が一因とされている。しかし匿名であれ実名であれ、怒りを言葉にして吐き出すと、かえって怒りが強まるという指摘もある。専門家は、感情をぶつける前に一晩置くことなど、非難の応酬を避ける具体策を挙げている。怒りを感じたら、まず返信せずに下書きに残す習慣も有効だとされる。
cards.en: Why do posts that revile complete strangers online never stop? Among researchers, the 'disinhibition effect,' in which not being seen weakens self-restraint, is considered one cause. But whether anonymous or under a real name, some also point out that putting anger into words and venting it can actually intensify it. Experts cite concrete measures to avoid exchanges of condemnation, such as letting a night pass before venting one's feelings. Leaving a draft unsent when anger arises is also said to be a helpful habit.

cards.enTarget: Why do posts that revile complete strangers online never stop?

words.defJa: 物事が実現しそうだという見通し

cards.ja: 長期の目標が重くのしかかるのは、終わりのめどが見えないときである。人は、完了までの道筋が描けないと、実際の作業量以上に疲れを感じる傾向がある。そこで効果的なのは、全体を小さな段階に分け、順序を決めて今日の分だけを確実に終わらせることだ。『ここまでやれば一区切り』と言える地点が増えるのに伴って、不安は少しずつ薄れていく。終わりが見えれば、人は驚くほど粘り強くなれるものである。
cards.en: A long-term goal weighs heavily when no prospect of an end is in sight. Unable to picture the path to completion, people tend to feel more tired than the actual workload warrants. What works, then, is to divide the whole into small stages, set an order, and reliably finish only today's portion. As the points where you can say 'done up to here' increase, anxiety gradually fades. Once the end comes into view, people can become astonishingly persistent.

words.defJa: うそや偽りで相手に本当でないことを信じさせる

cards.ja: 敬語は、うまく使えば人を和ませるが、使い方次第では人をだますこともできる。たとえば、『検討します』と言われて喜んだ人が、実は露骨な拒絶を避けるための婉曲な断りだったと後で知ることは珍しくない。丁寧な言葉ほど、本心を覆い隠す布になりやすいのである。それゆえ、日本語の読み手は、言葉そのものよりも言外の含みを読む力を磨いてきた。言葉の美しさと誠実さは、必ずしも比例しないのが厄介なところである。
cards.en: Honorific speech soothes people when used well, but depending on how it is used it can also deceive them. For example, it is not rare for someone delighted to hear 'I'll consider it' to learn later that it was a roundabout refusal meant to avoid blunt rejection. The more polite the wording, the easier it becomes a cloth that hides one's true feelings. For that reason, readers of Japanese have honed the ability to read implication rather than the words themselves. That beauty of words and sincerity do not necessarily go together is what makes it troublesome.

words.defJa: 鋭い目つきで相手をじっと見つめる

cards.ja: 瞑想を邪魔されたシヴァが、愛の神カーマを額の第三の目でにらむと、その体は一瞬で灰になったと伝えられる。この神話は、欲望が燃え尽きるさまを描いたものにほかならない。しかし物語には続きがあり、カーマは姿のない存在として、のちに別の姿で世界へよみがえる。欲望という頑固なものは、神といえども完全には消し去れず、形を変えて残る。そんな含みが、この短い神話の結末から静かに読み取れる。
cards.en: It is told that when Shiva, his meditation disturbed, glared at Kama, the god of love, with the third eye on his forehead, the body turned to ash in an instant. This myth is nothing other than a depiction of desire burning itself out. But the tale has a sequel, in which Kama, as a being without form, later comes back to the world in another form. Desire, being such a stubborn thing, cannot be wiped out completely, even by a god, and remains in changed form. That is the implication one can quietly read from the ending of this short myth.

cards.ja: 学生のころ、国語の授業をろくに聞いてなかったんですよ。それが大人になって日本語を勉強し直してみたら、頑固な文法嫌いだった私が、助詞の使い分けに夢中にならずにはいられなかったんです。きっと、点数のためじゃなくて、自分の言葉の仕組みを知りたいっていう動機があったからなんでしょうね。理由さえあれば、人って意外と机に向かえるものですよ。勉強する理由は、始めてから見つかることもあるんですよ。
cards.en: When I was a student, I hardly listened in Japanese class. But when I went back to studying Japanese as an adult, I, a stubborn grammar-hater, could not help getting absorbed in how particles are used. Probably it was because I had the motive of wanting to know how my own language works, not for a score. Give people a reason, and they can surprisingly sit down at a desk. Sometimes the reason to study only turns up after you've started.

words.defJa: よくない目的を達するために、ひそかに企てる

cards.ja: 『もっと上へ行きたい』という野心そのものが、悪いわけではありません。ただ、他人を出し抜こうともくろむとき、人の頭は驚くほど速く回り始めます。ところが、その計算には、相手がどう感じるかという視点がすっぽり抜け落ちているのです。うまく立ち回ったつもりでも、信頼を失って長期的には損をしかねません。本当に強い信頼関係は、相手にも得をさせようとする小さな積み重ねから生まれるのです。
cards.en: The ambition to climb higher is not itself a bad thing. But when someone schemes to outmaneuver others, the mind starts to race astonishingly fast. Yet in that calculation, the perspective of how the other person feels has dropped out completely. Even if you think you played it cleverly, you could lose trust and come out behind in the long run. Truly strong relationships of trust grow from small accumulations of trying to let the other person gain too.

words.defJa: 愛想がなく、冷たい感じのするさま

cards.ja: 人は、自分に向けられたそっけない返事に、驚くほど長く心を引きずられるものです。たった一言『了解』と返されただけで、嫌われたのではないかと夜まで考え込んでしまう。心理学では、これを人間が曖昧な情報を悪い方向に補う傾向として説明します。ただ、相手はただ忙しかっただけ、ということのほうがよほど多いのが現実です。だからこそ、解釈を急ぐことなく、事実と推測を分けて考える習慣が役に立ちます。
cards.en: People are surprisingly slow to shake off a curt reply aimed at them. Just one word, 'Understood,' sent back, and we brood until nightfall, wondering whether we are disliked. Psychology explains this as the human tendency to fill in ambiguous information in a negative direction. Yet in reality, it is far more often the case that the other person was simply busy. That is exactly why a habit of separating fact from guesswork, without rushing to interpret, proves useful.

words.defJa: 申し込みや応募などを、受け付けずに退ける

cards.ja: インドの公務員試験は、合格者の数が極端に限定されており、大半の受験者が最初の関門ではねられる。それでも毎年、多くの若者がこの狭き門に挑み続けている。背景には、公務員という地位が持つ、安定した収入と社会的な信用の高さがある。職を得れば、本人のみならず一族の暮らしまで変わると考えられているのだ。試験の準備に何年もかけ、複数回挑戦する人も少なくないとされ、その覚悟の重さがうかがえる。
cards.en: India's civil service exam admits an extremely limited number of successful candidates, and most examinees are rejected at the first hurdle. Even so, every year many young people keep challenging this narrow gate. Behind it lies the high social credibility that the status of civil servant carries. It is believed that landing a post changes not only one's own life but the lives of the whole extended family. Many are said to spend years preparing and to sit the exam several times, which shows how heavy their resolve is.

words.defJa: 条件や判断が厳しく、容赦のないさま

cards.ja: ジャイナ教の修行は、インドの諸宗教の中でもとりわけシビアなことで知られます。たとえば、小さな虫を踏まないよう、箒で道を掃きながら歩く修行者がいます。不殺生を徹底する姿勢は、食事から歩行に至るまで、日常のあらゆる動作に及んでいるのです。その厳しさの先にあるのは、自分の魂を行為の汚れから解き放つという目標です。そこまで徹底できるのは、教えが日々の生き方そのものと一体になっているからです。
cards.en: Jain practice is known as especially severe even among the religions of India. For example, there are ascetics who walk while sweeping the road with a broom so as not to step on small insects. The posture of thoroughgoing non-violence extends to every action of daily life, from eating to walking. Beyond that severity lies the goal of freeing one's own soul from the stain of action. They can go that far because the teaching is one with their daily way of living itself.

cards.enTarget: Jain practice is known as especially severe even among the religions of India.

words.defJa: 勢いよく外へ吹き出す

cards.ja: ヒマラヤの麓にあるインド北部の温泉地では、冷たく澄んだ朝の空気の中で、岩の割れ目から白い蒸気が噴く光景に出会う。周辺の聖地では、こうした現象を神の働きとして崇める習わしが今も続く。科学的には、地下の熱が水を温めて湧き出させていると説明できるが、人々はそこに、説明しきれない畏れも感じ取ってきた。自然の不思議と信仰が、ここでは日々の暮らしの中でひとつに溶け合っている。
cards.en: In a hot-spring town in northern India at the foot of the Himalayas, in the cold morning air, one comes across the sight of white steam spouting from cracks in the rock. In the surrounding holy places, the custom of revering such phenomena as the work of the gods continues even today. Scientifically it can be explained that underground heat warms water and makes it well up, but people have also sensed there an awe that cannot be fully explained. Here, the wonders of nature and faith melt into one within daily life.

cards.enTarget: In a hot-spring town in northern India at the foot of the Himalayas, in the cold morning air, one comes across the sight of white steam spouting from cracks in the rock.

words.defJa: あらかじめ用意した工夫やからくり

cards.ja: 歴史を語る名手は、聞き手の関心を引く仕掛けを、話の最初に置く。たとえば「本能寺の変の前夜、中国へ向かうはずだった軍勢が、なぜか京へ進路を変えた」と切り出せば、聞き手は、なぜ、と先を知りたくなる。答えをすぐに渡さず、疑問を持ち越させることが、その技の核心だ。そそっかしい聞き手でさえ、続きを待たずにはいられない。話の構成は、情報の順序を設計する仕事にほかならない。
cards.en: A master at telling history places a device that draws the listener's interest at the very beginning of the story. If he opens with, for example, 'On the eve of the Honnoji Incident, an army that was supposed to head for the western provinces changed course, for some reason, toward Kyoto', the listener wants to know what comes next, and why. Not handing over the answer at once, but making the question carry over, is the core of the technique. Even a careless listener cannot help waiting for the continuation. Structuring a story is nothing other than the work of designing the order of information.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「仕掛けを施す・置く」。聞き手の関心を引くために前もって用意した工夫。
cards.sense: からくり、前もっての工夫
cards.enTarget: A master at telling history places a device that draws the listener's interest at the very beginning of the story.

words.defJa: 胸や腹の中にある器官

cards.ja: お腹の調子が悪いと気分まで沈み、整うとほっとする。この当たり前の経験に、科学がようやく答えを出しつつあります。内臓の中でも腸には、数億ともいわれる神経細胞が網の目のように広がり、「第二の脳」と呼ばれることがあるのです。腸内細菌が気分に影響する可能性も、研究が進んでいる最中ですから、断定はできません。それでも、心と体を別物と考える昔ながらの見方は、すでに揺らぎ始めています。
cards.en: When your stomach is off your mood sinks too, and when it settles you feel relieved. Science is at last beginning to give an answer to this ordinary experience. Among the internal organs, the intestine in particular has nerve cells, said to number in the hundreds of millions, spread through it like a net, and it is sometimes called the 'second brain'. The possibility that gut bacteria affect mood is still in the middle of being researched, so no firm conclusion can be drawn. Even so, the old view that mind and body are separate things has already begun to waver.

cards.enTarget: Among the internal organs, the intestine in particular has nerve cells, said to number in the hundreds of millions, spread through it like a net, and it is sometimes called the 'second brain'.

words.defJa: 果たすべき務めがあるという意識

cards.ja: そういえば、うちの国語の先生、授業のたびに「言葉は人を傷つけも救いもする」って言ってたんですよ。国語を教える人だけあって、言葉に対する使命感がすごかったんです。最初は大げさだなと思ったけど、作文を返すときも、赤ペンの一言まで毎回本気でした。卒業して十年たった今、人にかける一言をふと選んでる自分がいて、ちょっと驚いてます。あの先生に、ちゃんと伝わってたんだなって、今さら思います。
cards.en: Come to think of it, my Japanese teacher used to say every class, 'Words can both hurt and save a person', you know. As someone who taught Japanese, his sense of mission about language was incredible. At first I thought it was exaggerated, but he meant it every time, down to the single line in red pen when he handed back our essays. Ten years after graduating, I sometimes catch myself choosing the words I say to people, and it surprises me a little. I think now, rather late, that his message really did get through to me.

cards.tipJa: 「使命感に燃える・駆られる」。自分に課された役目を果たそうとする強い意識。

words.defJa: ものごとが成り立つ構造や仕掛け

cards.ja: 言葉は、意味を運ぶ容器にすぎないのだろうか。私にはそうは思えない。助詞ひとつが文の重心を動かす仕組みを知れば、母語と外国語の垣根さえ低く見えてくる。たとえば「は」と「が」の違いは、辞書の訳語を並べても決して説明しきれず、話し手が何を既知とし、何を新しい情報として差し出すかという構造に根ざしている。外国語を学ぶとは、他人の言葉を覚えることである以前に、自分の言葉の骨組みを発見することにほかならない。
cards.en: Is language nothing more than a container that carries meaning? I cannot think so. Once you know the mechanism by which a single particle shifts the center of gravity of a sentence, even the hedge between your mother tongue and a foreign language begins to look low. The difference between wa and ga, for example, can never be fully explained by lining up dictionary translations; it is rooted in a structure of what the speaker treats as already known and what is offered as new information. To learn a foreign language is, before it is memorizing someone else's words, nothing other than discovering the framework of your own.

words.defJa: 人としての正しい道に関わるさま

cards.ja: 歴史の授業では、奴隷制や植民地支配のように、過去の人物の行いを現代の基準で裁いてよいか、という問いが出ることがある。倫理的な評価を下すこと自体は否定されないが、当時の制度や価値観、人々の置かれた状況を知らないまま裁けば、事実の理解を誤りかねない。まず何が起きたのかを、複数の史料に基づいて確かめ、そのあとで評価を考える。この順序を逆にすると危うい、というのが歴史学習の基本である。
cards.en: In history class, the question sometimes arises, over things like slavery and colonial rule, whether it is right to judge the deeds of figures of the past by present-day standards. Passing an ethical judgment is not itself denied, but if one judges without knowing the institutions, the values, and the circumstances people found themselves in at the time, one may well misunderstand the facts. First confirm what happened on the basis of multiple historical sources, and only afterward consider the evaluation. That reversing this order is precarious is a basic principle of studying history.

words.defJa: 形や意志が簡単に変わらないさま

cards.ja: 固い決意は、しばしば人を支えるが、同時に人を縛りもする。「三日坊主を二度としない」と誓った人ほど、一日でも休もうものなら、そこで全てが終わったと感じ、すべてを投げ出したくなる。その意味で、決意は岩のようにではなく、結んだ紐のように、ほどけても結び直せるしなやかさがあるほうが長持ちする。習慣を育てるとは、強さを競うことではなく、折れても何度でも戻ってくる力を養うことにほかならない。
cards.en: A firm resolve often supports a person, but at the same time it also binds them. The more a person has vowed 'never to be a three-day quitter again,' the more, if they so much as rest for a day, they feel that everything is over and want to throw it all away. In that sense, a resolution lasts longer if it is not like a rock but like a tied cord, supple enough to be retied even when it comes undone. Cultivating a habit is nothing other than nurturing the power to come back time and again even when broken, not competing in strength.

cards.en: Installing a dictionary app does not by itself make your Japanese improve. People who have mastered the tool always save each word they look up together with an example sentence and read it aloud again the next day. What matters here is not the number of features a tool has but the habit of repeating the same routine every day, whether tired or busy. If you forget features the moment you learn them, even the finest app becomes a treasure wasted. In the end, what counts is not the tool's performance but the user's routine.

cards.en: Generative AI has improved rapidly in performance, but the problem of plausibly stating things contrary to fact still remains. Companies are advancing countermeasures such as having systems consult search results, but they have not reached a complete fix, and the more specialized the field, the harder it is to spot errors. When businesses bring it into operations, the reality is that the more important the decision, the less they can do without a system of human verification. While expectations for accuracy rise, the question of where responsibility lies is also emerging.

cards.ja: AIに質問を入力すると、その内容が学習に使われることがあります。そのため企業では、顧客の個人情報や社外秘の資料の取り扱いについて、入力してよい範囲をあらかじめ社内ルールで決めておくのが普通です。そそっかしい社員が機密をうっかり入力してしまえば、それまでです。ただし、禁止一辺倒では、現場は黙って隠れて使い始めます。便利な道具ほど、使い方の約束が先に必要になるのです。
cards.en: When you enter a question into an AI, that content may be used for training. That is why companies normally decide in advance, in internal rules, the range of what may be entered concerning the handling of customers' personal information and confidential documents. If a careless employee inadvertently enters a secret, that is the end of it. Yet if the policy is nothing but prohibition, people on the ground will quietly start using it in secret. The more convenient the tool, the more a promise about how to use it is needed first.

Since it was a shot of my grandfather when he was young, I was a little moved when it came back to life in a few dozen seconds from a state riddled with cracks and faded color. I'm grateful that it fixes things, but it feels kind of complicated that even the time that was there gets wiped out. In the end, I decided not to leave everything to it and to put back by hand only the spots that bothered me.

What the listener wants to know is what, how far, and by when, and the strength of your feelings comes after that. Just because you spoke in a crisp, clear voice doesn't mean the substance gets across. Merely making your words concrete can make the same person trusted like a different individual. That's why, before giving an answer, I make a point of working in a single number.

cards.ja: 日本の学校では、黒板の板書をノートに写す授業が、伝統的なやり方として長く定着してきた。ところが近年、書きながら考えさせたり、友達と説明し合わせたりする方式を取り入れる学校も出てきている。背景にあるのは、写しただけで理解した気になるのは勘違いだ、という学習研究の蓄積である。とはいえ、板書を写す作業が集中を助ける場面もあり、従来の方法が無駄だったと断じるのは早計だろう。
cards.en: In Japanese schools, lessons in which students copy the blackboard into their notebooks have long been established as the traditional way. In recent years, however, some schools have begun to adopt methods in which students think while writing or explain things to friends. Behind this lies an accumulation of learning research holding that feeling you have understood merely because you copied something is a misunderstanding. Even so, copying the board can help concentration in some situations, so it would be premature to conclude that the older method was a waste.

words.defJa: 相手に強く願うときに使う丁寧な語

cards.ja: 江戸時代の百姓が代官に出した嘆願書を読むと、決まり文句の多さに驚きます。「何とぞ御慈悲を」と深く頭を下げ、凶作を理由に年貢の軽減を願い出る形が、ほとんど型になっているのです。とはいえ、へりくだるばかりではありません。村の窮状を石高や人数まで細かく書き連ねて、相手が断りにくい状況をつくろうともくろんでいたのです。言葉づかいは丁重でも、中身は意外なほど戦略的でした。
cards.en: Reading the petitions that Edo-period farmers submitted to their magistrates, you are struck by how many set phrases there are. The form of bowing deeply with an expression like 'kindly show your mercy' and requesting a reduction in the land tax on grounds of crop failure has become almost a template. Yet they were not merely humbling themselves. By setting out the village's plight in detail, down to crop yields and head counts, they schemed to create a situation in which it would be hard for the other side to refuse. The wording was courteous, but the substance was surprisingly strategic.

How fast you can prepare differs enormously depending on how many people you have who can explain the terminology, whether in medicine or in law. But just handing out business cards won't make those ties grow; only when experiences of having been useful to someone pile up one by one does it turn into trust. It's best to start by somehow seeing the work in front of you through.

cards.en: The Bhagavad Gita begins on a battlefield. On the eve of the great war at Kurukshetra, Prince Arjuna is crushed by the reality that he must fight even his kin and teachers, and lays down his bow. Facing the approaching catastrophe, he asks what the meaning of fighting is. Then Krishna, serving as his charioteer, teaches him to cast aside attachment to results and do his duty. It is a teaching about action and outcome that speaks even to the anxiety before an exam.

cards.en: Speech guidebooks all but unanimously urge you to sum up your points in three. Two looks like a contrast, and with four or more, little stays in the listener's head. Among odd numbers, three is perhaps the smallest unit of coherence, having a beginning, a middle and an end. Still, relying on this form too easily can breed the assumption that the content must fit into three. A form is a tool that helps thinking, not a shackle that binds it.

cards.ja: AIの規制をめぐる各国の姿勢は、驚くほど対照的だ。欧州連合は、リスクの大きさに応じて用途を分類する包括的な法律を成立させた。一方、米国は、業界の自主的な取り組みを重んじる傾向が強いと言われる。この違いは、速い技術の進歩に法律が追いつけるのか、また規制が新しい技術の芽を摘まないかという、根深い問いの表れでもある。どちらが妥当かという問いへの答えは、まだ出ていない。
cards.en: The stances of countries over AI regulation are strikingly contrasting. The European Union enacted a comprehensive law that classifies uses according to the size of the risk. The United States, on the other hand, is said to lean strongly toward respecting voluntary industry efforts. This difference also expresses a deep question: whether law can keep up with fast technological progress, and whether regulation might nip new technologies in the bud. The answer to which is appropriate has not yet emerged.

words.defJa: 決着がつかず中途半端な状態

cards.en: In technical talks, someone says "accuracy is ninety percent" and then the talk is left hanging in midair. What the audience wants to know is the real situation hidden in the remaining ten percent. A number becomes language only when paired with its meaning. The situation is the same for semiconductor yield and for model accuracy. Even if you hear a yield is eighty percent, the next move to make is wholly different depending on whether the remaining twenty percent are defective chips that failed inspection or chips that work but run slowly.

That is exactly why noticing it while it is still a small sprout matters above all. As with weeding a garden, putting in just a few minutes of work while the roots are shallow prevents big jobs later. This is also the reason for making a point of observing the movements of the mind in meditation every day.

cards.enTarget: Attachment spreads deep in the mind the way a tree sets roots in soil, and once settled it cannot be easily pulled out.

words.defJa: 欠点がまったくないこと

cards.ja: ダ・ヴィンチみたいに偉い芸術家でも、完璧を求めすぎて未完成のまま手放した作品がいくつもあるんですよ。《東方三博士の礼拝》なんかもそうです。依頼主を待たせたあげく、結局ミラノへ旅立ってしまったんですね。完成させるより次の興味に移る人だったんでしょうね。理想が高い人に言いたいんですけど、巨匠でさえ未完成と折り合いをつけながら次へ進んでいたんですから、もう少し肩の力を抜いていいと思うんですよ。
cards.en: Even a great artist like da Vinci left several works unfinished because he demanded perfection. The Adoration of the Magi is one such case. After keeping his client waiting, he ended up leaving for Milan. He was probably the kind of person who moved on to the next interest rather than finish. To those with high ideals, I'd say even a master went on to the next thing while making peace with the unfinished, so I think you can relax your shoulders a little.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: ダ・ヴィンチみたいに
がいくつもあるんですよ。《
ってしまったんですね。
んでいたんですから、もう
cards.tipJa: 「完璧を求める」「完璧主義」。欠点のなさを理想とする語。
cards.enTarget: Even a great artist like da Vinci left several works unfinished because he demanded perfection.

words.meaning: to fall out of use, to decline
words.defJa: 使われなくなって衰えること

cards.ja: ラジオ体操とか、毎朝やってた習慣って、気づいたら廃れてたりしません？あれ、意志が弱いというより、きっかけがなくなっただけなんですよね。夏休みに公園へ集まるっていう仕掛けがなくなれば、続ける理由も消えるわけで。習慣を残したいなら、気合いより先に、きっかけの置き場所を考えたほうがいいですよ。習慣も言葉も、使う場がなくなると、誰にも気づかれないまま静かに消えていくものなんですよ。
cards.en: Things like radio calisthenics, a habit you did every morning, haven't they fallen out of use before you noticed? That is less weak will than the trigger simply being gone. Once the setup of gathering in the park during summer vacation is gone, the reason to continue disappears too. If you want to keep a habit, think about where to place the trigger before you rely on willpower. Habits and words alike, once their place of use is gone, quietly vanish without anyone noticing.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

えたほうがいいですよ。
えていくものなんですよ。
cards.tipJa: 「習慣が廃れる」「伝統が廃れる」。使われず衰えていく。
cards.enTarget: Things like radio calisthenics, a habit you did every morning, haven't they fallen out of use before you noticed?

words.defJa: 仕組みや範囲が大きいこと

cards.ja: 国立国語研究所は、全国各地の方言を記録する大規模な調査を、長年にわたって続けてきた。若い世代ほど方言が薄れているとはいえ、語尾や抑揚には地域差が依然として残る。研究者たちは、消えつつある語彙を録音するとともに、使われ方の変化を追っている。調査の成果は、教育の現場や地域の言葉の保存にも役立てられている。言葉の変化は、辞書の改訂を待たずに、人々の暮らしの中で静かに、しかし確実に進んでいる。
cards.en: The National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics has for many years continued a large-scale survey that records dialects across the country. Although dialects are fading faster among younger generations, regional differences still remain in sentence endings and intonation. The researchers are recording vocabulary that is disappearing while also tracking changes in how it is used. The results are also put to use in schools and in preserving local speech. Language change does not wait for dictionary revisions; it proceeds quietly but surely within people's daily lives.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「大規模な調査・工事・災害」のように、規模の大きさを硬い文で述べる。
cards.enTarget: The National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics has for many years continued a large-scale survey that records dialects across the country.

words.defJa: おそろしいと感じて避けようとする

cards.ja: 新しい技術を怖がるのは、人間にとってごく自然な反応です。電卓が教室に入ってきた時代にも、計算力が落ちるのではないかと心配する先生や親の声がありました。恐れるあまり触れずにいると、使いこなす人との差が、気づかないうちに静かに開いていきます。かといって、AIの答えを何でも鵜呑みにするのも、同じくらい危険です。大事なのは、疑う目を持ちながらも、まず手を動かして小さく試してみる姿勢でしょう。
cards.en: Being afraid of a new technology is a perfectly natural human reaction. Even in the era when calculators came into classrooms, there were voices of teachers and parents worried that calculation ability would fall. If you avoid touching it out of fear, the gap with those who master it quietly opens without your noticing. That said, swallowing everything an AI says whole is just as dangerous. What matters is probably the attitude of keeping a doubting eye while still trying things out in small ways with your own hands.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: いていきます。かといって、AIの
cards.tipJa: 「新技術を怖がる」。「怖い」から作る動詞で、人の態度を述べる。
cards.enTarget: Being afraid of a new technology is a perfectly natural human reaction.

words.defJa: 心配が消えてほっとすること

cards.ja: 戦国の武将ってさ、勝つ側につくのは命がけだけに、読みを誤れば一族ごと消えるじゃないですか。関ヶ原のあと、領地を取り上げられずに済んだ大名は、心底安堵しただろうなって思うんですよ。逆に、西軍についた毛利は大きく減らされたわけで、この差が後の幕末まで響くんです。勝ち負けの実情は、いつも紙一重なんですよね。歴史の教科書には出てこない、そういう人間くさい感情を想像すると、急に面白くなりませんか？
cards.en: Warlords of the Sengoku era, you see, risked their lives choosing the winning side, so one misjudgment could wipe out a whole clan. I imagine the daimyo who were not stripped of their domains after Sekigahara felt deep relief. Mori, on the other hand, sided with the Western Army and was cut down sharply, and that gap echoes all the way to the end of the shogunate. The reality of winning and losing is always a hair's breadth apart. Doesn't it suddenly get interesting when you imagine such human feelings that never show up in textbooks?

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「安堵の息をつく」「胸をなで下ろして安堵する」。ほっとする気持ち。
cards.enTarget: I imagine the daimyo who were not stripped of their domains after Sekigahara felt deep relief.

words.defJa: 表からは見えにくい本当の事情

cards.ja: 生成AIの普及に伴い、データセンターの電力消費が各国で問題になっている。ただ、実情を正確に示す統計はまだ少なく、事業者ごとの公表も限られる。そのため、電力会社や自治体は、見通しの立てにくい状況での設備計画を余儀なくされている。省エネ型の半導体の開発は、その対策の一つとして期待されている。足元の数字が十分にそろわないうちは、拙速な結論を避け、慎重に議論を進める姿勢が求められる。
cards.en: With the spread of generative AI, power consumption by data centers has become a problem in many countries. Yet statistics that accurately show the actual situation remain scarce, and disclosure by operators is limited. As a result, utilities and municipalities are forced to plan facilities under hard-to-predict conditions. The development of energy-saving semiconductors is expected to be one countermeasure. Until the figures at hand are sufficiently in, an attitude of avoiding hasty conclusions and proceeding carefully with debate is called for.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「実情を把握する・に合わせる」のように、現場の本当の事情を指す。
cards.enTarget: Yet statistics that accurately show the actual situation remain scarce, and disclosure by operators is limited.

words.defJa: 使い道がなく捨てられるもの

cards.ja: 十九世紀のロンドンは、人口の急増に伴って、し尿や工場の廃棄物がテムズ川に流れ込む街でした。1858年の夏には、耐えがたい悪臭が議事堂まで届き、「大悪臭」と呼ばれる事態になります。これを機に、技師バザルジェットが大規模な下水道網をつくり、街の衛生は大きく改善しました。この事業は、都市のインフラが人の命を守ることを示した代表的な例です。ロンドンの経験は、衛生が都市の課題として意識される転機となりました。
cards.en: Nineteenth-century London, with its rapidly growing population, was a city where sewage and factory waste flowed into the Thames. In the summer of 1858, an unbearable stench reached Parliament in what came to be called the Great Stink. Taking this as the occasion, the engineer Bazalgette built a large-scale sewer network, and the city's sanitation improved greatly. This project is a representative example showing that urban infrastructure protects human lives. London's experience became a turning point at which sanitation came to be recognized as an urban issue.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「産業廃棄物」「廃棄物処理」。捨てられるものを総称する。
cards.enTarget: Nineteenth-century London, with its rapidly growing population, was a city where sewage and factory waste flowed into the Thames.

words.meaning: to keep in mind, to make a point of
words.defJa: いつも気をつけて努めること

cards.ja: ヨーガ・スートラは、心の揺れを静める方法として、修習と離欲の二つを挙げる。修習とは、静けさを保つ努力を、日々の平凡な反復の中で長く続けることである。離欲とは、見聞きするものへの執着から離れようと心がけることにほかならない。どちらか一方だけでは足りず、車の両輪のように働いてこそ、心は落ち着きを得る。修習と離欲の釣り合いという視点は、情報にあふれた現代の暮らしにも、そのまま通じる教えといえよう。
cards.en: The Yoga Sutras list two methods for stilling the mind's fluctuations: practice and non-attachment. Practice is continuing the effort to keep stillness over a long time in ordinary daily repetition. Non-attachment is nothing other than making a point of leaving behind attachment to what is seen and heard. Neither alone is enough; only when they work like the two wheels of a cart does the mind find calm. The viewpoint of balancing practice and non-attachment can be called a teaching that applies as it is even to modern life, overflowing with information.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: ことにほかならない。どちらか
cards.tipJa: 「〜しようと心がける」。日ごろから意識して努める。
cards.enTarget: Non-attachment is nothing other than making a point of leaving behind attachment to what is seen and heard.

words.defJa: 日が暮れて暗くなりかける頃

cards.ja: 窓の外に夕闇が降りてくる頃、研究室の画面では、学習の誤差がまだ下がり続けていました。この仕組みを知らずに欲張ってモデルを大きくすると、過学習に陥りかねません。止めどきを見極めるのも、立派な技術です。経験を積んだ研究者ほど、派手な新手法を試す前に、この地味な見極めへ時間をかけるものです。夜が更けるにつれ、部屋に残っているのは、計算機の唸りだけになっていきました。
cards.en: As dusk settled outside the window, the training error on the lab screen was still dropping. If you enlarge the model greedily without knowing this mechanism, you may well fall into overfitting. Knowing when to stop is also a real skill. The more experienced the researcher, the more time they spend on this plain judgment before trying a flashy new method. As the night deepened, all that remained in the room was the hum of the computers.

cards.tipJa: 「夕闇が迫る・降りる」の形で、日暮れの薄暗さを表す文章語。
cards.enTarget: As dusk settled outside the window, the training error on the lab screen was still dropping.

words.defJa: 客を迎えて応対するための部屋

cards.ja: 初対面の相手を応接室で待つ間、人は想像以上に、こちらの様子を観察されている。入室の瞬間に何を言うかより、座る姿勢や資料の置き方、余計な動きの少なさが、印象を左右することも多い。話し方を磨く前に、まず黙っている時間の過ごし方を整えておくといい。入室の前に深呼吸を一つして、手元の資料の順番を確かめるだけで、動作は驚くほど落ち着くものだ。第一声は、その静けさの延長にすぎない。
cards.en: While waiting in a reception room for someone you meet for the first time, you are being observed more than you imagine. More than what you say the moment you enter, your sitting posture, how you place your documents and how few needless movements you make often sway the impression. Before polishing how you speak, it is good to first prepare how you spend the silent time. Just taking one deep breath before entering and checking the order of your documents makes your movements calm down surprisingly. Your first words are merely an extension of that stillness.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「応接室に通す」。客を迎える部屋。会社や学校で使う。
cards.enTarget: While waiting in a reception room for someone you meet for the first time, you are being observed more than you imagine.

words.defJa: いくつにも分かれて広がること

cards.ja: 世界史が苦手だという人は、出来事の膨大さに圧倒されているだけです。たとえば大航海時代ひとつとっても、航海術や香辛料の貿易はもちろん、宗教や銀の流通まで、話題は多岐に及びます。ばらばらに覚えるのではなく、まず大まかな原因と結果の糸でつなぐのがコツです。糸が一本通れば、暗記の量は驚くほど減ります。地図の上で、点ではなく線で歴史を追う癖がつくと、新しい時代に出会っても慌てずに済みます。
cards.en: People who say they are bad at world history are often simply overwhelmed by the sheer number of events. Take the Age of Discovery alone: the topics range widely, from navigation and the spice trade to religion and the flow of silver. The trick is not to memorize things separately but first to connect them with a rough thread of cause and effect. Once one thread runs through, the amount you have to memorize drops surprisingly. Once you get into the habit of following history as lines rather than points on a map, you will not panic when you meet a new era.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: されているだけです。たとえば
でつなぐのがコツです。
cards.tipJa: 「多岐にわたる」「多岐に及ぶ」の形で、分野や内容の広がりを表す。
cards.enTarget: Take the Age of Discovery alone: the topics range widely, from navigation and the spice trade to religion and the flow of silver.

words.defJa: 元のものに正確に従う様子

cards.ja: 翻訳は、原文に忠実であろうとするほど、訳文が不自然になるという矛盾を抱えている。機械翻訳が進歩した今も、この緊張は依然として消えていない。言葉の意味は、辞書の中ではなく、文化の背景と文脈に宿るがゆえである。本当の正確さとは、単語を一対一で置き換えることではなく、読み手に同じ効果を生むことなのかもしれない。訳者の腕は、辞書に載っていない部分の判断でこそ、いちばん試されるのである。
cards.en: Translation harbors the contradiction that the more it tries to be faithful to the original, the more unnatural the translated text becomes. Even now that machine translation has advanced, this tension has still not disappeared. This is because the meaning of words dwells not in the dictionary but in cultural background and context. True accuracy may be not replacing words one to one but producing the same effect in the reader. A translator's skill is tested most in judgments about the parts that are not in the dictionary.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: むことなのかもしれない。
cards.tipJa: 「原文に忠実」「事実に忠実」。元のものから離れず正確に従う。
cards.enTarget: Translation harbors the contradiction that the more it tries to be faithful to the original, the more unnatural the translated text becomes.

words.defJa: 細部にこだわらず全体をとらえる様子

cards.ja: 辞書が示す語義は、言葉の動きを大まかに区切った地図にすぎない。実際の用法は、その境界を平気でまたぎ、文脈ごとに色を変えていく。地図を暗記したところで、旅をしたことにはならないのと同じである。ゆえに、言葉の習得とは、語義の暗記ではなく、用例の中を巡ることにほかならない。辞書を引く目的は、正解を確かめることより、言葉の輪郭が揺れる場所を見つけることにあるのではないか。
cards.en: The senses a dictionary lists are merely a map that divides the movement of words roughly. Actual usage casually crosses those borders and changes color with each context. Memorizing a map does not mean you have made a journey. Hence, acquiring a language is not memorizing senses but nothing other than traveling through examples. Perhaps the point of consulting a dictionary lies less in confirming the right answer than in finding the places where a word's outline wavers.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: をしたことにはならないのと
ることにほかならない。
つけることにあるのではないか。
cards.tipJa: 「大まかに区切る」「大まかな流れ」のように、細部を捨てて全体をつかむ意味。
cards.enTarget: The senses a dictionary lists are merely a map that divides the movement of words roughly.

words.defJa: 物事を調べ解くきっかけとなるもの

cards.ja: AIの回答を読むときは、結論だけでなく、どんな手がかりをもとにその答えに至ったのかを探るとよい。根拠が示されていなければ、もっともらしい文章でも信用に足るとは言えないからだ。安易に信じ込むのは危うい。同じことは人前で話す場面にも当てはまり、聞き手は話し手の根拠の出し方を見て信頼を決める。答えの出どころをたどる癖を毎日の習慣にするだけで、AIとの付き合い方は目に見えて変わってくる。
cards.en: When reading an AI's answer, it is wise to probe not just the conclusion but what clues led it to that answer. Without stated grounds, even a plausible text cannot be called worthy of trust. Believing it easily is dangerous. The same applies when speaking in public, where listeners decide how far to trust a speaker by how the speaker presents evidence. Merely making a daily habit of tracing where an answer comes from visibly changes how you deal with AI.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: されていなければ、もっともらしい
cards.tipJa: 「手がかりをつかむ」「手がかりになる」。解決への糸口を指す。
cards.enTarget: When reading an AI's answer, it is wise to probe not just the conclusion but what clues led it to that answer.

words.defJa: 長く親しんで離れがたい気持ち

cards.ja: ガンジス河畔の古都ヴァーラーナシーには、何千年も同じ場所で祈り続けてきた人々がいます。彼らの土地への愛着は、単なる郷愁ではありません。仏教が「執着は苦をもたらす」と説いたのは、まさにこうした強い結びつきの裏側を見ていたからです。教理はさておき、寺院の鐘の音に涙する人を責める気には私はなれません。祈りの場をめぐる人々の物語に耳を傾けることも、インド哲学を理解する大切な入口だと私は思います。
cards.en: In Varanasi, the old city on the Ganges, there are people who have gone on praying in the same place for thousands of years. Their attachment to the land is no mere nostalgia. Buddhism taught that clinging brings suffering precisely because it saw the dark side of such strong bonds. Doctrine aside, I cannot bring myself to blame someone who weeps at the sound of a temple bell. Listening to people's stories about their places of prayer is also, I think, an important entrance to understanding Indian philosophy.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: ヴァーラーナシーには、
いたのは、まさにこうした
cards.tipJa: 「愛着がわく」「愛着を感じる」。物や場所への親しみに使う。
cards.enTarget: Their attachment to the land is no mere nostalgia.

words.defJa: 長く続いて治りにくい性質

cards.ja: 日本語学習者の悩みで多いのが、助詞の「は」と「が」の使い分けが慢性的に曖昧なままだってことなんですよ。何年も勉強してきたものの、いつまでたっても自信がつかない。実はこれ、文法書を丸暗記するだけでは直らなくて、談話の流れの中で感覚をつかむ必要があるんです。ですから、まずは身近な会話の標本を集めてみるといいですよ。その中で「は」と「が」がどう選ばれているかを観察すれば、規則の裏にある感覚が見えてきます。
cards.en: One of the most common worries among learners of Japanese is that their grasp of when to use the particles wa and ga stays chronically vague. They have studied for years, yet confidence never comes. In fact this will not be fixed by memorizing a grammar book; you need to get a feel for it within the flow of discourse. So start by collecting specimens of everyday conversation. If you observe how wa and ga are chosen in them, the feel behind the rules will come into view.

ruby: なままだってことなんですよ。
してきたものの、いつまでたっても
があるんです。ですから、まずは
めてみるといいですよ。その

cards.enTarget: One of the most common worries among learners of Japanese is that their grasp of when to use the particles wa and ga stays chronically vague.

words.defJa: やるぞという強い気持ち

cards.ja: インドの哲学を日本に伝えた先人たちの意気込みには、頭が下がります。たとえば明治の仏教学者、南条文雄はオックスフォードに渡り、サンスクリット語を学び抜いた人物です。当時は梵語の文献を読める日本人など、ほとんどいませんでした。それでも彼は帰国後、経典の校訂を通じて、日本の仏教研究の基盤を築いたのです。その地道な努力がなければ、私たちが今日、日本語でインドの原典に触れることはもっと難しかったに違いありません。
cards.en: I bow my head before the zeal of the forerunners who brought Indian philosophy to Japan. Take the Meiji Buddhist scholar Nanjo Bunyu, who went to Oxford and studied Sanskrit through to the end. At the time, almost no Japanese could read Sanskrit texts. Even so, after returning home, he laid the foundation of Japanese Buddhist research through his editing of the scriptures. Without that steady effort, it would surely be far harder for us today to touch Indian original texts in Japanese.

など、ほとんどいませんでした。それでも
cards.tipJa: 「意気込みを見せる」「強い意気込みで」の形で、やる気や決意を表す。
cards.enTarget: I bow my head before the zeal of the forerunners who brought Indian philosophy to Japan.

words.defJa: わざとそうすること

cards.ja: ルネサンス期のイタリアでは、故意に事実を歪めて書かれた歴史書がいくつも存在しました。たとえば有力な家に雇われた書き手は、主人の先祖を実際以上に立派に描くのが仕事だったのです。そうした文章は、当時の権力者の自己像を知る貴重な資料にもなります。歴史家は、書かれた内容のみならず、誰が何のために書いたのかを問うのです。史料の裏にある意図を読み解く作業は、探偵の仕事にどこか似ているのです。
cards.en: In Renaissance Italy there existed a number of history books written by deliberately distorting the facts. Writers hired by powerful families, for example, had the job of portraying their master's ancestors as better than they really were. Such writings also become valuable material for knowing how the powerful of the day saw themselves. Historians ask not only what is written but who wrote it and for what purpose. Deciphering the intentions behind a source is somehow similar to a detective's work.

cards.tipJa: 「故意に〜する」「故意か過失か」。わざとであることを示す語。
cards.enTarget: In Renaissance Italy there existed a number of history books written by deliberately distorting the facts.

words.defJa: 政府に近い関係者のこと

cards.ja: 「政府筋によると」という書き出しの記事は、読者に独特の読み方を求める。発言者の名前が伏せられているため、情報の確度を自分で見極めざるを得ないからだ。観測気球として意図的に流された話か、実際に決まった方針かを区別する手がかりは、複数の報道を突き合わせることにある。記事の大小にかかわらず、出どころの見えない情報ほど、受け取る側の冷静さが問われる。報道を読む側にも、情報を疑う力と待つ余裕が必要になる。
cards.en: Articles that open with according to government sources demand a particular way of reading. Because the speaker's name is withheld, readers have no choice but to judge the reliability of the information themselves. The clue to telling a trial balloon deliberately leaked from a policy actually decided lies in comparing several reports. Regardless of the size of the article, the less visible the source, the more calm is asked of the recipient. Readers of the news also need the power to doubt information and the patience to wait.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「政府筋によると」。名前を出さない政府関係者の情報源を示す報道語。
cards.enTarget: Articles that open with according to government sources demand a particular way of reading.

words.defJa: 人々の前で見せたり知らせたりすること

cards.ja: 勉強の成果を人前で披露する機会があると、記憶は驚くほど定着します。インドの伝統的な師弟教育では、長きにわたって、弟子が師の前で聖典を暗唱してみせる場面が重んじられてきました。完璧に再現できなくても、覚えたことを声に出す行為そのものが想起練習になります。ただ詰め込むだけの勉強より頭に残るのは、そのためでしょう。人前で話す緊張感こそが、記憶を引き出す練習を本物にしてくれるのです。
cards.en: When you have a chance to show your study results in front of people, memory settles in surprisingly well. In traditional Indian teacher-pupil education, for a very long time the scene of a pupil reciting scripture before the master has been prized. Even if the recitation is not perfect, the act of saying aloud what you learned is itself retrieval practice. That is probably why it sticks better than mere cramming. It is precisely the tension of speaking before others that makes the practice of drawing out memory real.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: るのは、そのためでしょう。
cards.tipJa: 「芸を披露する」「結婚披露宴」。多くの人に見せ知らせる場面。
cards.enTarget: When you have a chance to show your study results in front of people, memory settles in surprisingly well.

words.defJa: 情報を集めるためのつながり

cards.ja: AIのニュースって、結局SNSで流れてくるものを追ってるだけじゃないですか。でも本当に早い人は、半導体の新工場の話を公式発表の三日前に知っていたりするんですよ。ああいう人は、業界のあちこちにつながる独自の情報網を持っているに違いありません。検索だけに頼っている自分が、案外のんびりしているように思えてきます。しかもそういう人ほど、情報をもらうだけでなく自分からも惜しみなく差し出しているんですよね。
cards.en: AI news is mostly just whatever floats by on social media, isn't it? But the truly fast people sometimes learn about a new chip plant three days before the official announcement. Such people must have their own information network, connected to every corner of the industry. Relying only on search, I start to feel surprisingly slow. What's more, such people don't just receive information; they hand it out generously themselves.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.enTarget: Such people must have their own information network, connected to every corner of the industry.

words.defJa: これ以上は進めない最後のぎりぎり

cards.ja: 人は極限状態に置かれたとき、何を支えに生き延びるのか。精神科医のヴィクトール・フランクルは、強制収容所での体験をもとに『夜と霧』を著し、人間には最後まで「態度を選ぶ自由」が残ると述べました。食べ物も尊厳も奪われるなかで、彼は意味の欠如こそが人を最も深く蝕み、意味への意志が人を支えると見たのです。この考えは、現代の心理療法にも大きな影響を与えています。だからこの本は、今も多くの人に読み継がれています。
cards.en: When people are placed in extreme conditions, what do they rely on to survive? The psychiatrist Viktor Frankl wrote Man's Search for Meaning on the basis of his experiences in concentration camps and stated that humans retain to the end the freedom to choose their attitude. Even as food and dignity were stripped away, he saw the lack of meaning as what eats away at a person most deeply and the will to meaning as what sustains them. This idea has had a great influence on modern psychotherapy. That is why this book is still read by many people today.

えています。だからこの
cards.tipJa: 「極限状態」「体力の極限」。これ以上耐えられない限界を指す。
cards.enTarget: When people are placed in extreme conditions, what do they rely on to survive?

words.defJa: すっかり腐って形が崩れる

cards.ja: かつて栄えた半導体工場が、使われないまま朽ち果てる例も少なくない。技術の世代交代は速く、一つ前の製造ラインは数年で採算に合わなくなるからだ。とはいえ、旧世代の装置でも、車や家電向けの成熟した製品を作る役割はまだ残っている。「最先端」だけを見ていると、この産業を支える基盤が見えなくなってしまう。古い工場の跡地が研究施設や物流拠点に生まれ変わる例もあり、産業の寿命は一つの形では終わらない。
cards.en: There are not a few cases of once-thriving chip factories rotting away unused. Generations of technology turn over fast, and the previous production line stops paying within a few years. Even so, older-generation equipment still has a role in making mature products for cars and home appliances. If you look only at the cutting edge, you lose sight of the foundation that supports this industry. There are also cases where old factory sites are reborn as research facilities or logistics hubs, so an industry's life doesn't end in a single form.

cards.tipJa: 「朽ち果てた小屋」。長い年月で完全に崩れ傷む様子を表す。
cards.enTarget: There are not a few cases of once-thriving chip factories rotting away unused.

words.defJa: 出しゃばらず、ひかえめな様子

cards.ja: インドの人って、遠慮しないで何でも言うイメージがあったんだけど、実際に会ってみたら案外控え目な人も多かったよ。特にお寺で出会ったおばあさんは、質問しても声が小さくて、こっちが聞き返してしまうほどだった。でも、ひとたび仏様の話になると、目が輝いて止まらなくなるんだよね。ああいう静かな熱には、心に迫るものがあるんだよね。声の大きさだけでは、その人の熱量は測れないのだと、あのとき初めて気づいたんだ。
cards.en: I had this image of Indians as people who say whatever they like without holding back, but when I actually met them, plenty turned out to be surprisingly reserved. In particular, an old woman I met at a temple spoke so softly, even when asked questions, that I had to ask her to repeat herself. But once the talk turned to the Buddha, her eyes lit up and she couldn't stop. There is something that gets to your heart in a quiet fervor like that. It was then that I first realized you can't measure a person's passion by the loudness of their voice.

してしまうほどだった。でも、ひとたび
まらなくなるんだよね。ああいう

cards.tipJa: 「控え目な態度」「控え目に言う」。出しゃばらず量や程度を抑える。
cards.enTarget: I had this image of Indians as people who say whatever they like without holding back, but when I actually met them, plenty turned out to be surprisingly reserved.

words.defJa: 物や状態を悪くしてしまう

cards.ja: 指導者の不誠実な一言は、国全体の信頼を損なうことがある。歴史を振り返れば、約束を重んじなかった権力者の多くが、その代償を戦乱という形で払っている。信頼とは一度に築けるものではなく、小さな誠実さの積み重ねでしか育たない。それゆえに、失うときの速さは、築く労苦に比べてあまりにも残酷である。一方、誠実な約束を守り続けた指導者は、時代が下っても人々の記憶の中で敬意をもって語られる。
cards.en: A leader's single dishonest remark can damage the trust of a whole nation. Looking back through history, many rulers who did not honor their promises paid the price in the form of war. Trust is not something that can be built at once; it grows only through an accumulation of small acts of sincerity. For that very reason, the speed with which it is lost is all too cruel compared with the labor of building it. By contrast, leaders who kept faithful promises are spoken of with respect in people's memory even as the ages pass.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「信頼を損なう」「健康を損なう」。価値や状態を悪くする意味。
cards.enTarget: A leader's single dishonest remark can damage the trust of a whole nation.

words.defJa: あるべきものが足りないこと

cards.ja: 歴史家の間では、ヴァイマル共和国の崩壊を、民主主義を支える国民的な合意の欠如から説明する見方が根強い。一九二九年の世界恐慌に伴って失業者が急増し、議会は有効な対策を打ち出せなかった。やがて極端な主張が支持を広げ、三三年にはナチ党が政権の座に就く。もっとも、崩壊の原因を一つに絞ることには、慎重であるべきだとする研究者も多い。歴史は、一つの原因ではなく、いくつもの偶然と選択の重なりとして動いていく。
cards.en: Among historians, the view that explains the collapse of the Weimar Republic by a lack of the national consensus supporting democracy remains strong. With the Great Depression of 1929, the number of unemployed rose sharply, and parliament could not come up with effective countermeasures. Before long extreme claims spread their support, and in 1933 the Nazi Party took the seat of power. Still, many researchers say we should be cautious about narrowing the cause of the collapse down to one thing. History moves not through a single cause but as an overlapping of many accidents and choices.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「責任感の欠如」「欠如している」。あるべきものがない状態。
cards.enTarget: Among historians, the view that explains the collapse of the Weimar Republic by a lack of the national consensus supporting democracy remains strong.

words.defJa: 死んだ人とけがをした人

cards.ja: 大惨事が起きると、報道はまず死傷者の数を伝える。しかし数字の大小はさておき、数字だけではひとりひとりの人生が見えなくなる危うさがある。心理学者は、被害者が増えるほど人の共感が薄れる「心理的麻痺」という現象を指摘してきた。数字の裏にある個人を想像する努力が、受け手の側にも求められている。亡くなった人の数ではなく、その一人ひとりの名前を伝える報道が、記憶を長く支えることもある。
cards.en: When a great disaster occurs, the news first reports the number of casualties. But setting aside whether the number is large or small, numbers alone carry the danger of making each individual life invisible. Psychologists have pointed out a phenomenon called psychic numbing, in which the more victims there are, the more people's empathy fades. The effort to imagine the individuals behind the numbers is also asked of the audience. Reporting that conveys not the number of dead but each person's name can also sustain memory for a long time.

ruby: だけではひとりひとりの
cards.tipJa: 「死傷者が出る」「死傷者数」。事故や災害の報道でよく使う語。
cards.enTarget: When a great disaster occurs, the news first reports the number of casualties.

words.defJa: 多くの人や出来事の中で鍛えられる

cards.ja: 外国語を学ぶ人のあいだで、「現地で揉まれる」ことの効果が改めて注目されている。教室で習った表現が通じない場面に何度も出会うと、学習者は相手の反応を見て言い方を修正せざるを得なくなる。そうした試行錯誤の積み重ねが、教科書にはない生きた言語感覚を育てるという。とはいえ、極限まで追い込まれるような環境が誰にでも合うとは限らない。短い滞在でも、現地の人と毎日言葉を交わす環境に身を置けば、上達の速さが違ってくるという声は多い。
cards.en: Among people learning foreign languages, the effect of being knocked about on location is drawing fresh attention. When learners repeatedly meet situations where classroom expressions don't work, they have no choice but to watch the other person's reaction and adjust how they speak. Such accumulated trial and error is said to cultivate a living sense of language that textbooks lack. That said, an environment that pushes you to the limit does not suit everyone. Many say that even a short stay changes how fast you improve if you put yourself in an environment of exchanging words with locals every day.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「世間に揉まれる」「人混みに揉まれる」。苦労して鍛えられる意味。
cards.enTarget: Among people learning foreign languages, the effect of being knocked about on location is drawing fresh attention.

words.defJa: 結婚している人

cards.ja: 婚活アプリにとって、既婚者の登録をどう見抜くかは長年の課題です。申告をそのまま信じるだけでなく、書き込みの矛盾を機械学習で検出する案も考えられます。ただ、こうしたシステムを作るにあたっては、利用者のプライバシーを損なわないかが壁になります。技術的にできるからといって、何でも調べてよいわけではありません。結局のところ、守るべきなのは規約よりも、そこで出会う人々の信頼なのでしょう。
cards.en: For dating apps, how to spot registrations by married people has long been a challenge. Besides simply trusting what users declare, one idea is to detect contradictions in their posts with machine learning. However, in building such a system, whether it harms users' privacy becomes the obstacle. Just because something is technically possible does not mean everything may be investigated. In the end, what must be protected is not the rules but the trust of the people who meet there.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

にできるからといって、

cards.tipJa: 「既婚者」と「未婚者」。結婚している人を指す語で、書類や調査で使う。
cards.enTarget: For dating apps, how to spot registrations by married people has long been a challenge.

words.defJa: 物事を良い方向に考えるさま

cards.ja: 話し手が楽観的に聞こえるかどうかは、内容よりも声の調子で決まることが多い。語尾を少し上げ、間を短くすると、同じ言葉でも前向きな印象になる。逆に、声を落として控え目な声量で間を長くとれば、慎重で誠実な空気が生まれる。場面に応じてどちらを伝えたいのかを決めてから話し始めるだけで、聞き手の受け取り方は大きく変わるはずだ。声の使い方は、生まれつきの才能ではなく、意識すれば誰でも磨ける技術である。
cards.en: Whether a speaker sounds optimistic is often decided more by tone of voice than by content. If you raise the end of a sentence slightly and shorten the pauses, even the same words give a positive impression. Conversely, if you lower your voice, speak at a modest volume and hold longer pauses, a careful and sincere atmosphere arises. Just by deciding, according to the occasion, which one you want to convey before you start speaking, the way listeners take it should change greatly. How you use your voice is not an innate talent but a skill anyone can hone with awareness.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「楽観的な見方」「楽観的に考える」。物事を明るく見る様子。
cards.enTarget: Whether a speaker sounds optimistic is often decided more by tone of voice than by content.

words.defJa: 政治や社会で大きな力を握る人

cards.ja: AIが発達すると、結局一番得するのは権力者なんじゃないかって、よく言われるじゃないですか。監視カメラと顔認証を組み合わせれば、昔の王様が夢見た情報網が手に入るわけですからね。でも、技術を使う側が好き勝手できるどころか、社会のルールに縛られる場面も多いんですよ。結局は技術そのものより、誰がどう使うかの問題なんです。だからこそ、技術を監視する市民の目をどう確保するかが、これからの大きな論点になってきます。
cards.en: People often say that as AI develops, those in power will end up benefiting most, don't they? After all, combine surveillance cameras with face recognition and you get the information network that kings of old dreamed of. But far from being able to do as they please, those who use the technology are often bound by society's rules. In the end it is a question not of the technology itself but of who uses it and how. That is why how to secure citizens' eyes to watch the technology is becoming a major issue from now on.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: なんじゃないかって、よく
われるじゃないですか。
るわけですからね。でも、
cards.tipJa: 「権力者に逆らう」「時の権力者」。政治的な力を握る人。
cards.enTarget: People often say that as AI develops, those in power will end up benefiting most, don't they?

words.defJa: 暮らしに必要な費用

cards.ja: ムンバイでは、地方から働きに来た人々の多くが、懸命に働いて得たわずかな収入を、生活費と故郷への送金に振り分けている。家賃の高さは国内でも知られ、狭い共同の部屋で暮らす例も少なくない。それでも人口は増え続け、都市は出稼ぎの労働者に支えられて動いている。政府は低所得者向けの住宅整備を進めているが、需要には追いつかない状況である。物価の上昇が続けば、故郷への仕送りを減らさざるを得ない世帯も出てくるだろう。
cards.en: In Mumbai, many of the people who came from rural areas to work divide the small income they earn by hard work between living expenses and remittances to their hometowns. High rents are well known even within the country, and not a few live in cramped shared rooms. Even so, the population keeps growing, and the city runs on the labor of migrant workers. The government is advancing housing for low-income people, but it cannot keep up with demand. If prices keep rising, some households will have no choice but to cut the money sent home.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「生活費を稼ぐ・切り詰める」。家賃・食費など暮らしにかかる費用の総称。
cards.enTarget: In Mumbai, many of the people who came from rural areas to work divide the small income they earn by hard work between living expenses and remittances to their hometowns.

words.defJa: 前もっての計画がないさま

cards.ja: 家計の相談窓口には、無計画に買い物を重ねて月末に資金が足りなくなる、という相談が絶えないとされる。買った直後は満足しても、時間がたつと不要だったと気づく例が多い。専門家は、買う前に一日置くだけで衝動が薄れると助言する。生活費の固定分を先に取り分けておけば、残りは自由に使えるため、罪悪感も生まれにくい。計画とは、我慢を強いるどころか、自由に使える範囲を守るための設計である。
cards.en: Household-budget counseling desks are said to get a steady stream of people who buy on impulse and run short of money by the end of the month. Right after buying they are satisfied, but as time passes many realize they did not need the item. Specialists advise that merely waiting a day before buying thins out the impulse. If you set aside the fixed portion of living costs first, the rest can be spent freely, so guilt is less likely to arise. A plan is not a demand for self-denial but a design that protects the range you can spend freely.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「無計画に〜する」「無計画な旅行・出費」。計画の欠如を責める語感。
cards.enTarget: Household-budget counseling desks are said to get a steady stream of people who buy on impulse and run short of money by the end of the month.

words.defJa: 続けざまに起こる

cards.ja: ここ十数年、ネットを舞台に、短くて勢いのある新語が相次いで生まれては消えている。年配の人はそれを「言葉の乱れ」と嘆くが、言語学の目から見れば、変化は言葉が生きている証拠である。実際、いまでは当たり前の「めっちゃ」や「うざい」も、かつては若者言葉として眉をひそめられた。流行語の多くは一時の現象にすぎないが、生き残った語は、人々の暮らしに根を下ろして日本語になる。言葉への愛着は、古さへの執着とは別のものである。
cards.en: For the past decade or so, short, punchy new words have been appearing one after another online, only to vanish. Older people lament this as a corruption of language, but from the viewpoint of linguistics, change is proof that a language is alive. In fact, mecha and uzai, now taken for granted, were once frowned on as youth slang. Most buzzwords are no more than a passing phenomenon, but the ones that survive put down roots in people's lives and become Japanese. Affection for a language is a different thing from clinging to its old forms.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: の「めっちゃ」や「うざい」も、かつては
cards.tipJa: 「事故・不祥事が相次ぐ」。同種の出来事が続くとき、「相次いで」の形が多い。
cards.enTarget: For the past decade or so, short, punchy new words have been appearing one after another online, only to vanish.

words.defJa: 海外などへ派遣される記者

cards.ja: 一九四七年、インドがイギリスから独立してパキスタンと分かれたとき、世界各地の新聞社が現地に特派員を送りました。彼らの記事は、独立の祝賀だけでなく、故郷を離れることを余儀なくされた、一千万人を超えるともいわれる人々の姿も伝えています。現場の混乱は、記録の細部にまで刻まれているのです。当時の紙面を読むと、数字の背後にある一人ひとりの顔が見えてきます。歴史の手がかりは、公式文書に限らないのです。
cards.en: In 1947, when India won independence from Britain and split from Pakistan, newspapers around the world sent correspondents to the scene. Their articles convey not only the celebration of independence but also the people, said to number over ten million, who were forced to leave their homes. The chaos on the ground is etched into the details of the record. Reading the papers of the time, you begin to see the individual faces behind the numbers. Clues to history are not limited to official documents.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

cards.tipJa: 「海外特派員」「特派員が伝える」。新聞社やテレビ局が現地に派遣する記者。
cards.enTarget: In 1947, when India won independence from Britain and split from Pakistan, newspapers around the world sent correspondents to the scene.

words.defJa: 色や味、感じがうすいさま

cards.ja: 日本語には、色の薄さを表す言葉が驚くほどたくさんあります。中でも「淡い」は、色に限らず、期待や記憶のように輪郭のはっきりしないものにも使える便利な言葉です。恋心や悲しみにこの言葉を添えると、とたんに儚い響きが生まれます。「薄い」や「浅い」にはない、この余韻に、日本語を話す人は愛着を覚えるのでしょう。和歌から現代の歌詞に至るまで、この一語は移ろいやすい心を静かに描いてきました。
cards.en: Japanese has a surprising number of words for the paleness of colors. Among them, awai is a handy word that applies not only to color but also to things with blurry outlines, like hopes and memories. Add it to love or sorrow and a fleeting, wistful tone appears at once. Speakers of Japanese probably feel an attachment to this lingering note that the words for thin and shallow lack. From waka to modern song lyrics, this one word has quietly portrayed the shifting heart.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）

ruby: くほどたくさんあります。
のはっきりしないものにも
cards.tipJa: 色だけでなく「淡い期待」「淡い恋」など、はかない感情にも使う。
cards.enTarget: Among them, awai is a handy word that applies not only to color but also to things with blurry outlines, like hopes and memories.

words.defJa: 感情に流されず筋道で判断するさま

cards.ja: 十八世紀のヨーロッパで啓蒙思想が広がるに伴って、人間は理性的に考えさえすれば、迷信や権威から自由になれるという期待が高まりました。ヴォルテールやカントといった思想家がその旗手で、科学の目覚ましい進歩も、この楽観を後押ししました。しかし、フランス革命のあとの恐怖政治は、理性の名のもとにも多くの血が流れうることを示しました。理性への信頼と、その危うさへの自覚。この二つが同居しているのが、近代という時代の特徴です。
cards.en: As the Enlightenment spread across eighteenth-century Europe, expectations rose that humans could free themselves from superstition and authority if only they thought rationally. Thinkers such as Voltaire and Kant were its standard-bearers, and the remarkable progress of science also boosted this optimism. But the Terror after the French Revolution showed that much blood could be shed even in the name of reason. Trust in reason, and awareness of its dangers. The coexistence of these two is the mark of the modern age.

src.site: 書き下ろし（このデッキ用）
